title: Basic Statistics
notes: Beginner course, no prior experience needed; covers descriptive statistics, distributions and sampling. Certificate is paid; free access options vary on the page.

title: Data and statistics (6th grade: mean, median and mode)
notes: Gentle unit with videos and practice on calculating mean, median and mode and how outliers shift them; for absolute beginners.

title: Exploring data: Graphs and numerical summaries
notes: Level 1 course on histograms and numerical summaries: median, mean, standard deviation, IQR and resistant measures; free badge/statement on completion.

title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics (18.05)
notes: Undergraduate course with notes, problem sets and R tutorials on distributions, confidence intervals and inference; needs calculus.

title: Introductory Statistics 2e, Chapter 2: Descriptive Statistics
notes: Free textbook chapter on quartiles, percentiles, mean/median/mode, variance, standard deviation and box plots; suits learners who want worked examples.

title: Mean, Median, and Mode: Measures of Central Tendency: Crash Course Statistics #3
notes: Short video on how mean, median and mode differ, what their relationship reveals, and how averages can mislead.

title: OpenIntro Statistics
notes: Free PDF textbook with videos, slides and labs; covers summarizing data, distributions, sampling and inference.

title: Prices, location and spread
notes: Level 1 introductory course using price data to teach median, mean, weighted averages, interquartile range and boxplots.

title: STAT 500: Applied Statistics
notes: Open (CC BY-NC) course notes reviewing probability, common distributions and statistical methods at graduate-refresher level.

title: Statistical Thinking for the 21st Century
notes: Free online book covering summarizing data, skew and long-tailed distributions, variability, sampling error and the bootstrap.

title: Statistics - A Full University Course on Data Science Basics
notes: 8-hour free video course (article page embeds it) covering central tendency, variation, percentiles, box plots and the normal distribution.

title: Statistics 110: Probability
notes: Harvard course site (free lecture videos and free online textbook) on probability and distributions; rigorous foundation for variation and sampling.

title: Statistics Done Wrong
notes: Free online guide to common statistical errors including small samples, power and misleading summaries; assumes no prior statistics.

title: Statistics for Applications (18.650)
notes: Rigorous undergraduate course with lecture videos on the mathematical foundations of estimation and statistical methods; for strong quantitative learners.

title: Summarizing quantitative data
notes: Unit on mean vs median, range, IQR, standard deviation and identifying outliers, with practice exercises; suits beginners to early learners.

title: Think Stats 2e
notes: Free Python-based book exploring real datasets: distributions, summary statistics, outliers and estimation; for learners comfortable with code.

title: Calling Bullshit: video lectures
provider: University of Washington (Carl Bergstrom and Jevin West)
notes: Ten lectures including correlation and causation, statistical traps, publication bias and fake news; for learners who know the basics.

title: Causal Diagrams: Draw Your Assumptions Before Your Conclusions
notes: 9-week course using causal diagrams to identify confounding and bias; free audit, verified certificate paid.

title: Causal Inference: The Remix (The Mixtape)
notes: Free online textbook on causal inference for social sciences: DAGs, potential outcomes, RDD, IV, diff-in-diff, synthetic control.

title: Causal Inference: What If
notes: Free textbook on causal inference from observational data and trials, with code in R, SAS, Stata, Python and Julia.

title: Correlation Doesn't Equal Causation: Crash Course Statistics #8
notes: Short video on correlation vs causation, scatter plots and why co-movement does not prove cause; beginner friendly.

title: Critical Evaluation in Data Science: Data, the World, and You
notes: 6-week course on spotting misleading statistics, sampling, variability and study design; limited free access, paid upgrade for full access.

title: How Not To Run an A/B Test
notes: Article on why repeatedly peeking at significance inflates false positives in A/B tests, with fixes.

title: Improving your statistical inferences
provider: Eindhoven University of Technology (Coursera, Daniel Lakens)
notes: Covers p-values, effect sizes, power, publication bias and experimental design; free to audit, certificate paid.

title: A/B Testing
notes: Free five-lesson course on designing and analysing online A/B tests, metrics, ethics and power; beginner level.

title: Introduction to Causal Inference
notes: Free 14-week lecture course on potential outcomes, causal graphs, randomized experiments and more; needs basic probability.

title: Making Sense of Data in the Media
notes: 3-week course on evaluating statistics in the media, correlation vs causation and sampling error; limited free access, paid upgrade for certificate.

title: Making Sense of Statistics
notes: Plain-language guide to numerical and statistical traps in news reporting, free PDF; written for journalists and general readers.

title: Sampling Methods and Bias with Surveys: Crash Course Statistics #10
notes: Short video on good vs bad survey questions, how samples are chosen, and sources of bias and error.

title: Spurious Correlations
notes: Browsable charts of coincidental correlations that show why correlation alone does not imply causation; good for beginners.

title: Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments: A Practical Guide to A/B Testing
notes: Paid book on rigorous large-scale A/B testing and pitfalls; chapter 1 free to download.

title: Types of statistical studies (practice)
notes: Khan Academy Study design unit exercise on telling experiments from observational and sample studies; part of a unit that also covers sampling bias and experiment design.

title: Using statistics in your research
provider: OpenLearn (Open University) / University of Wales Trinity Saint David
notes: Five-minute introduction to common misuses of statistics and the difference between correlation and causation; suits absolute beginners.

title: Bayes theorem, the geometry of changing beliefs
notes: Visual explanation of base rates, priors and updating with test-style problems; for learners comfortable with percentages.

title: Bayes' theorem of conditional probability (Wireless Philosophy)
notes: Short video on Bayes' theorem and the base rate fallacy (ignoring how common something is to begin with).

title: Calling Bullshit: Data Reasoning in a Digital World
notes: Free course syllabus and readings incl. effect sizes, Fermi estimation, base-rate fallacy, Bayes' rule and misleading proportions.

title: Chapter 15: Interpreting results and drawing conclusions (Cochrane Handbook)
notes: Expert guidance on risk ratios, relative and absolute risk reduction, risk difference, NNT and baseline-risk dependence; assumes some statistics background.

title: Get ready for ratios, rates, and percentages
notes: Preparatory unit reviewing multiplication, division and graphing before ratios, rates and percentages; suits learners starting from scratch.

title: Helping Doctors and Patients Make Sense of Health Statistics
provider: Psychological Science in the Public Interest (Gigerenzer et al.)
notes: 2007 landmark review on relative vs absolute risk, natural frequencies and base rates in screening; PubMed record, free full-text copies exist.

title: Introduction to Percents
notes: Plain-language intro to percent as per 100 with visual grids and conversions between percents, decimals and fractions; for absolute beginners.

title: Know Your Chances: Understanding Health Statistics
notes: Woloshin, Schwartz and Welch: reading risk numbers, absolute vs relative change and risk charts; free under Creative Commons.

title: Rates and percentages (6th grade)
notes: Rates, percent meaning, and converting between percents, fractions and decimals with practice; free.

title: Rates and percentages (7th grade)
notes: Percent word problems: discounts, tax, tips, markup and multi-step ratio and percent problems; free practice for learners who make frequent errors.

title: Ratio, Proportion and Percentages
notes: Level 1 introductory course: simple ratios, fractions/decimals/percentages, finding percentages, percentage increase and decrease; free statement of participation.

title: Ratios and rates (Pre-algebra)
notes: Proportional relationships, ratios, unit rates and rate problems with guided practice; free.

title: Survival Statistics: Secrets for Demystifying Numbers
notes: 3-week course (about 3 hours a week) on absolute vs relative risk, confusing percentages, rare events and surveys; FutureLearn access may be time-limited.

title: Think Bayes 2
notes: Free computational Bayesian statistics book with Jupyter notebooks; for strong learners wanting rigorous work on priors and base rates.

title: Unit rates and percentages
notes: Unit rates and percentages building on equivalent ratios, with practice exercises; free.

title: Analyzing categorical data
notes: Unit with videos and practice on reading and interpreting bar graphs and two-way tables; guided practice for learners making frequent errors.

title: Bar chart (Statistics: Power from Data!, section 5.2)
notes: Government guide to vertical, grouped, horizontal and stacked bar charts with real data; sibling pages cover pie, line, scatterplot and histogram.

title: Bar Graphs
notes: Plain-language explanation of bar graph parts, axes and values starting at zero, with examples and links to line graphs and pie charts.

title: Caveats: a collection of graphic pitfalls
notes: 30+ chart pitfalls with visual examples: pie charts, axis cutting, dual axes, bin sizes, overplotting, Simpson paradox.

title: Charts Are Like Pasta - Data Visualization Part 1: Crash Course Statistics #5
notes: About 10-minute video on bar charts, pie charts, pictographs and histograms, what they show and how they can mislead.

title: CSEP 590a Data Visualization
notes: University course with public lecture videos on visual encoding, perception, colour and uncertainty; assumes some technical comfort.

title: Data Visualization (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign)
notes: Beginner course on design and human perception principles for choosing effective visual displays; free to audit, paid certificate.

title: Financial Times Visual Vocabulary
notes: Reference poster and guide to chart types by purpose (deviation, correlation, distribution, time, part-to-whole); good for interpreting less common charts.

title: Fundamentals of Data Visualization
notes: Free online book on how data maps to visual properties, proportional ink, colour pitfalls and uncertainty displays.

title: How Charts Lie: Getting Smarter about Visual Information
notes: Paid book on how charts mislead through design, dubious data, hidden uncertainty and misleading patterns.

title: How to spot a misleading graph
notes: Short animated lesson on how graphs can be used carelessly or dishonestly and what to check.

title: Reading bar graphs
notes: Short video showing how to read values off a bar graph; suits absolute beginners.

title: Tools: Misleading axes on graphs
notes: Explains zero baselines for bars vs lines, dual axes, log vs linear scales and inverted axes.

title: Visualization Analysis and Design
notes: Rigorous framework for visual encoding and design; book is paid but the author site offers free lecture videos (6.5+ hours) and slides.

title: Working with charts, graphs and tables
notes: Introductory course on reading tables, percentages, pie and bar charts, histograms and line graphs; free statement of participation.

title: 15.279 Management Communication for Undergraduates
notes: Strategic professional communication: analysing audience, purpose and context, including cross-cultural communication.

title: 15.280 Communication for Managers
notes: Graduate-level workshop materials on strategic communication, writing and speaking for managers.

title: 15.281 Advanced Communication for Leaders
notes: Graduate materials on presenting to hostile audiences, executive summaries and interpersonal communication for leaders.

title: Business English for Cross-cultural Communication
notes: Beginner course on spotting cross-cultural misunderstandings and adapting business writing and speaking.

title: Effective communication in the workplace
notes: 8-week introductory course; Week 5 on adapting written style to audiences and Week 7 on communicating across culture and generations.

title: Getting to Si, Ja, Oui, Hai, and Da
notes: Erin Meyer on reading cultural context when negotiating and persuading across borders; subscriber content.

title: Harnessing the Science of Persuasion
notes: Cialdini's classic HBR article on six principles of persuasion for leaders; subscriber content.

title: High-Impact Business Writing
notes: Beginner course on emails, presentations and reports for business audiences; free to audit, paid certificate.

title: How to Brief a Senior Executive
notes: HBR article (US$11.95) on communicating with senior leadership and delivering executive briefings.

title: Influencing People
notes: Influence tactics and building informal power with peers, superiors and stakeholders; free to audit.

title: Knowing Your Audience (Business Writing)
notes: Short guide to adjusting tone, format and content to audience characteristics such as position and familiarity.

title: Speaking and Presenting: Pitches and Persuasion
notes: Crafting persuasive messages and pitching ideas to different audiences; free to audit.

title: Successful Negotiation: Essential Strategies and Skills
notes: Popular negotiation course covering framing and influence in business communication; graded work needs paid certificate.

title: The Culture Map: Breaking Through the Invisible Boundaries of Global Business
notes: Eight-scale framework for how culture shapes communicating, persuading and giving feedback; companion mapping tools.

title: Tone in Business Writing
notes: Concise guide to choosing confident, courteous, reader-focused tone and handling negative messages.

title: Workplace Communication Basics
notes: Short beginner course on verbal, listening and written workplace communication; good first step for absolute beginners.

title: Write Professional Emails in English
notes: Beginner course on email formats, tone and formality, including how culture affects what is appropriate.

title: Writing Better E-Mails
notes: Short course on polite, concise, professional email writing and etiquette for addressing recipients.

title: Business Writing
notes: Beginner course on organizing business documents, structure, grammar and revision for clarity.

title: Communicating in Technical Organizations (21W.780)
notes: Undergraduate course materials on email, document forms, style, collaborative writing and oral presentation in organizations.

title: Plain Language Guide Series
notes: Government guides on plain language principles, writing for understanding, design and testing clarity with readers.

title: Politics and the English Language
notes: Classic 1946 essay on vague, padded and stale prose and rules for writing plainly; free to read.

title: Professional Business Writing Skills
notes: Beginner video course on formatting sentences and paragraphs, structuring emails, proposals and reports, and proofreading.

title: Professional, Technical Writing
notes: Free reference pages on effective workplace writing, audience, memos, reports, tone and revision.

title: Steven Pinker - The Sense of Style at McGill University 2014/10
provider: YouTube (Steven Pinker talk at McGill University)
notes: Cognitive-science-based talk on classic style, the curse of knowledge and writing clearly for readers.

title: Style: Lessons in Clarity and Grace (13th edition)
provider: Pearson (Joseph M. Williams and Joseph Bizup)
notes: Rigorous method for diagnosing and revising unclear prose, concision and cohesion; paid textbook.

title: Successful Presentation
notes: Beginner course on a structural formula for presentations, verbal delivery and audience focus; covers spoken structure.

title: Technical Writing One
notes: Short self-study course on clear, concise sentences, active voice, lists, paragraphs and audience; stated pre-class time about 96 minutes.

title: Technical Writing Two
notes: Drafting and self-editing tactics, document organization and visuals; recommended after Technical Writing One (about 71 minutes pre-class).

title: The Elements of Style
notes: Public-domain classic on concise, direct prose and usage rules; free ebook.

title: The Pyramid Principle: Logic in Writing and Thinking (3rd edition)
notes: Definitive text on answer-first pyramid structure for business writing and thinking.

title: Building Self-Confidence Through Assertiveness
notes: Passive vs aggressive vs assertive communication, handling criticism and rejection, saying what you need; suits beginners.

title: Conflict Resolution Skills
notes: Beginner 6-hour course: active listening, communication styles, positions vs interests, building a conflict management plan.

title: Dealing with Difficult People and Situations
notes: Beginner course on communicating with hostile people and handling tough situations; types of difficult people, questioning and problem-solving steps.

title: Difference and challenge in teams
notes: Short introductory OpenLearn course on disagreement, assertiveness vs cooperation and collaborative resolution instead of compromise.

title: Difficult Conversations: How to Discuss What Matters Most
notes: Harvard Negotiation Project classic (3rd ed. 2023): the three conversations, managing emotion and identity, hard feedback and bad news.

title: Free Course: Managing Difficult Conversations at Work
notes: About 51 minutes of video: conversational fear, I-statements, tactical pausing, reframing hostility, repairing relationships after conflict.

title: Getting Past No: Negotiating in Difficult Situations
notes: Ury's strategy for staying in control under pressure, defusing anger and turning resistance into joint problem-solving.

title: How to have constructive conversations (Julia Dhar)
notes: Debate champion's TED talk on three features of productive disagreement: seeking progress rather than victory.

title: How to use others' feedback to learn and grow (Sheila Heen, TEDx)
notes: Harvard Negotiation Project researcher on receiving hard feedback well; companion to Thanks for the Feedback.

title: Introduction to Negotiation: A Strategic Playbook for Becoming a Principled and Persuasive Negotiator
notes: Barry Nalebuff's course with interactive negotiations; includes advanced topics such as negotiating with no power; free audit available.

title: Mediation and Conflict Resolution
notes: Intermediate course on mediation fundamentals in workplace and international contexts; free to audit.

title: Negotiation and Conflict Management (15.667)
notes: Graduate-level free course materials: negotiation styles, role-play simulations, difficult situations, first- and third-party conflict handling.

title: Negotiation Fundamentals
notes: Beginner course on negotiation strategy, preparation, value creation and process management; free to audit.

title: Power and Negotiation (15.665)
notes: Graduate-level free materials on negotiation theory and practice with simulations, exercises and cases.

title: Radical Candor: Kim Scott's feedback framework
notes: Free overview of caring personally while challenging directly, with the four quadrants for giving critical feedback.

title: Thanks for the Feedback: The Science and Art of Receiving Feedback Well
notes: Frameworks for responding to criticism with curiosity rather than defensiveness; for experienced professionals.

title: Working in groups and teams
notes: Free 8-hour OU Level 3 course; includes a section on managing conflict with five conflict-response styles and win-win approaches.

title: 10 ways to have a better conversation (Celeste Headlee)
notes: Practical conversation rules from a radio host: listen more, ask open questions, stay present.

title: 5 ways to listen better (Julian Treasure)
notes: TEDGlobal 2011 talk introducing conscious listening and the RASA method (receive, appreciate, summarize, ask).

title: Active Listening (practice guide)
provider: Greater Good Science Center, UC Berkeley
notes: Research-backed practice: paraphrasing, clarifying questions, empathy; at least 10 minutes, weekly practice.

title: Active Listening: Enhancing Communication Skills
notes: Beginner course on active listening, empathy, nonverbal cues and rapport; certificate is paid.

title: Coaching and Mentoring Skills for New Managers
notes: Short course on asking better questions, listening deeply and holding coaching conversations as a new manager.

title: Coaching Conversations
notes: Scenario-based course applying active listening and constructive feedback in manager-led coaching conversations; paid certificate.

title: Empathy and Emotional Intelligence at Work
provider: UC Berkeley Greater Good Science Center (edX)
notes: Research-led course on empathy and emotional intelligence in workplace relationships; free audit, $199 verified certificate per GGSC page.

title: Essential Soft Skills: Listening
notes: Beginner video course (1.5-3 hours stated) on active listening, focus and retaining information; paid certificate optional.

title: Feeling Heard: Experiences of Listening (or Not) at Work
notes: Open-access qualitative study of what makes employees feel heard beyond active-listening techniques; research-level reading.

title: Mastering Active Listening in the Global Workplace
notes: Intermediate course on reflective listening, empathy and adapting listening across cultures; certificate is paid.

title: The importance of interpersonal skills
notes: Short introductory course on interpersonal skills and how good communication shapes working relationships.

title: The Power of Listening at Work (Kluger and Itzchakov)
provider: Annual Review of Organizational Psychology and Organizational Behavior (author PDF via Leibniz Psychology)
notes: Academic review of listening outcomes, measurement and moderators at work; author-posted PDF, expert-level.

title: The Surprising Power of Questions
notes: Brooks and John on question types, follow-up questions and tone; HBR is subscription/metered.

title: What Great Listeners Actually Do
notes: Zenger and Folkman research on what top listeners do (questions, supportive interaction); HBR is subscription/metered.
